newsitem.title: USA: Hamas leader said to end fight against extradition.
newsitem.headline: Hamas leader said to end fight against extradition.

text.p: A Palestinian militant accused in Israel of murder and other violent acts is to give up his effort to resist extradition from the United States, the State Department said on Tuesday.
"We understand that Mr (Mousa Mohammed) Abu Marzook intends to withdraw his legal challenge to the order finding him extraditable," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"Any such legal decision is of course within Mr Abu Marzook's rights. It's entirely his own choice," Burns said.

Israel announced in 1995 that it had formally asked the United States to hand over Abu Marzook, who was arrested in July of that year at a New York airport as he flew to the United States where he had lived for many years.

Israel alleged that he was responsible, as head of the political arm of the Islamic resistance movement Hamas, for attacks that killed scores of Israelis. It did not contend that he had personally carried out violent acts.
Abu Marzook argued that he had been involved only in political matters, which are not extraditable offences.
A U.S. district judge ordered his extradition last May, saying he was involved in an "agreement to accomplish an unlawful act." The ruling was upheld by another judge in October.
Abu Marzook had appealed the rulings and, according to federal prosecutors, a U.S. government response to his appeal had been due Wednesday.
No further details were immediately available.
